findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is redefined as `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` is an `abc.ABC` with four abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. None of them are implemented here, so the class retains its `__abstractmethods__` and any attempt to construct it raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler ...`. `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) instantiates the registered handler unconditionally, so `process_detectors()` will blow up for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` instead of the previous no-op (`evaluate` returning `[]`). Either keep a concrete stub implementation of the four abstract members or leave the handler on the non-stateful `DetectorHandler` base until the real implementation lands.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still describes a list return value
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. There will be one result for each group key result in the packet". The same wording is misleading for implementers of the abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract, which also changed to a dict. Update the docstring to describe the dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: Stale TODO comment about stateful detectors
findings.body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` sits directly above a class that now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`, so the abstraction already exists and the TODO is misleading. It should be removed or replaced with the actual remaining work (implementing the abstract methods).

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests can't detect wrong arguments to the new hook
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` takes `value` but never uses it when constructing the `IssueOccurrence`, and the returned occurrence/event_data only depend on `group_key` and `new_status`. As a result the assertions in `TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results_multi_group` (line 190 passes `6` for `group_2`, whose actual value is `10`) and in `TestEvaluate`/`TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue` (which pass `6` while the data packets contain `100`, `8`, `200`, `10`) pass regardless of what value `evaluate_group_key_value` actually forwards to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. The main new behaviour of this PR — forwarding the correct group value and priority to the occurrence hook — is therefore untested. Encode `value` (e.g. in `evidence_data` or `subtitle`) and pass the real values in the assertions.

findings.title: get_group_key_values type annotation disallows the `None` group key that is actually used
findings.body: `get_group_key_values` is annotated as returning `dict[str, int]`, but `evaluate()` feeds those keys straight into `get_state_data`/`evaluate_group_key_value`, which are typed with `DetectorGroupKey` (`str | None`), and the new tests exercise exactly that case (`DataPacket("1", {"dedupe": 2, "group_vals": {None: 6}})`). The mismatch means type checking will not catch implementations that return `None` keys (legitimate) or will force implementers to lie about the type. Annotate it as `dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]`.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError when a detector declares no counters
findings.body: `counter_updates` is only populated inside `if self.counter_names:`; when a `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass legitimately declares `counter_names = []`, the dict stays empty and `counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]` raises `KeyError` for every group key. Since this PR documents/encourages new `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclasses (and adds a required `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook), it would be worth defaulting to `counter_updates.get(gk, {})` so counter-free detectors work.

findings.title: process_detectors return type changed from list to dict of results without updating consumers
findings.body: `process_detectors` now returns `list[tuple[Detector, dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]]]` instead of a list of results per detector. Any existing call site that does `for result in detector_results:` keeps working syntactically but silently iterates group keys (strings/None) instead of `DetectorEvaluationResult` objects, which fails only later and confusingly. Confirm all callers of `process_detectors()`/`DetectorHandler.evaluate()` outside this diff were updated to the dict contract.
